chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: May we combine Maghrib and 'Isha' while in residence before the sun disappears, without any excuse? He said: "There is no harm."

key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence; being settled and not traveling
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer
key_terms.عِلَّةٍ: a legal excuse or justifying cause
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.نَجْمَعُ: we combine, referring to performing two prayers together

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine Maghrib and 'Isha' in residence without an excuse according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling regarding the permissibility of combining the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers in residence without a specific excuse. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in doing so, indicating allowance in this matter within the framework of salat timings.
